public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI spent $8.67 billion on inference in the first nine months of 2025, undermining claims that its inference is profitable.

statement.excerpt: Some have been mighty confident about inference being profitable (due to a $7.5 billion cost of revenue on $13.07 billion in revenue), but overlooked my reporting from last year verified by the Financial Times showed OpenAI spent $8.67 billion on inference in the first nine months of 2025.

our_interpretation: The spending period is January 1 through September 30, 2025, in calendar years.
The accounting basis is estimate because the claim relies on press reporting of private records rather than an identified accounting standard.
The central numerical assertion requires the reported $8.67 billion amount and matching inference scope, not a rounded total-compute figure.

The profitability implication requires comparable revenue and costs for the same period and customer scope. Nine-month inference spending cannot simply be compared with annual revenue or annual cost of revenue.
The claim that the Financial Times verified the reporting is separate from other publications repeating Zitron's figure.
criteria.support_condition: Independent records or genuinely corroborating reporting establish $8.67 billion of OpenAI inference expenditure during January–September 2025. The profitability implication additionally requires matching revenue and a reconciliation of inference expenditure with accounting cost categories.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a materially different nine-month inference amount or show that the reported figure includes other costs. Comparable positive inference economics would contradict the profitability implication without necessarily contradicting the spending figure.
